mappings.note: Which work one should set the mind on (the easy one) -- a specific point located in the kundaliya. Rejected LO-72, the skim-for-usefulness outcome.

Names Giridhar's verse form, the kundaliya -- recognising the traditional oral form the poems are cast in, which is the closest the frame comes to appreciating folk verse. Rejected LO-73: the form is not a point inside the text.
Meaning of the archaic 'pachhtaay'. Rejected LO-73: lexical, not a search in the verse.
What the thoughtless man's mind lacks (chain, ease) -- located in the line. Rejected LO-70: the word is given, not the idea argued.
What follows acting without thought (regret). Rejected LO-70: the consequence is stated outright.
What the world does (laughs) -- located in the line. Rejected LO-70: stated.
Meaning of 'bisaari' (to forget) -- an archaic form. Rejected LO-73: lexical.
Meaning of 'manahin' -- the old oblique of 'man'. Rejected LO-73: lexical.
What sort of act the poet says a thoughtless one is -- his proposition in general terms. Rejected LO-73: the options generalise beyond any single line.
Which century the poet belongs to -- placing the text and its author. Rejected LO-73: not found inside the verse.
Of whom the world's laughter is said -- located in the verse. Rejected LO-70: attribution, not appraisal.
Sense of 'kaam bigaare aapano' -- the archaic possessive 'aapano' is the difficulty. Rejected LO-73: a phrase gloss.
What the poet says to forget (the past) -- located in the line. Rejected LO-70, kept for the items that ask what follows from forgetting it.

The chief mark of Giridhar's language -- plain, direct, close to the spoken folk tongue. That is an appreciation of the folk idiom of the verse, which this outcome covers. Rejected LO-76: the item judges a whole style, not a word.
Meaning of 'taahi mein chitt dei' -- an old phrase to be glossed. Rejected LO-73: lexical.
What follows from forgetting the past and looking ahead -- the poet's claim. Rejected LO-73: an argued consequence.
Which conviction ('parteeti') the poet urges -- his central idea. Rejected LO-76: the word is glossed in the stem itself.
How long painful experience troubles one, per the poet -- his proposition. Rejected LO-73: the options generalise beyond the line.
The purpose of the poems (moral instruction) -- their usefulness. Rejected LO-70: the item asks what they are for, not what he thinks.
Blank is 'samujhi', an archaic participle -- the form is the difficulty. Rejected LO-73, kept for blanks that are ordinary words.
Blank is 'dukh' -- an ordinary noun, so the item is verse recall. Rejected LO-76: no lexical difficulty.
Blank is 'yahai', the archaic emphatic pronoun. Rejected LO-73: the old form is the demand.
Blank is 'aapano', the archaic possessive. Rejected LO-73 on the same ground.
Blank is 'chitt' -- a word used throughout, so recall. Rejected LO-76: no new form.
Blank is 'sahaj' -- the poem's key term, already familiar. Rejected LO-76: recall rather than gloss.
Blank is 'bani', an archaic verb stem in 'bani aavai'. Rejected LO-73: the form is the demand.
Blank is 'khatkat', an archaic present participle. Rejected LO-73 on the same ground.
What happens when work is spoilt (the world mocks) -- located in the verse. Rejected LO-70: stated.
How many lines a kundaliya has -- knowledge of the traditional form itself. Rejected LO-73: the count is a fact about the genre, not a point in the text.
When a person becomes a laughing stock -- the verse says when he acts without thought. Rejected LO-70: stated.
Where the poet was born (Avadh) -- biographical placement. Rejected LO-73: not inside the verse.
Why the mind finds no ease -- the cause given in the verse. Rejected LO-70: stated.
The result of acting without thought -- spoilt work and regret, both in the verse. Rejected LO-70: located.
Which pleasures lose their savour -- food, honour, revelry, listed in the line. Rejected LO-76: the item asks the list, not the words' sense.
What one should do after forgetting past failures -- the poet's prescription. Rejected LO-73: a general course of action, not a located fact.
Who wrote 'beeti taahi bisaari de' -- attribution of the composition. Rejected LO-73: bibliographic.
What kind of work one should choose ahead -- the poet's counsel. Rejected LO-73, used for the bare 'which work' MCQ.
The result of unconsidered work -- spoilt work, regret, mockery, unrest, all in the verse. Rejected LO-72: the consequences, not the poem's use.
What the poet says about the past -- forget it and attend to what is ahead. Rejected LO-73: his position rather than a found detail.
Which pain 'khatkat hai jiy maahin' conveys -- the force of an archaic phrase. Rejected LO-70: a phrase, not a proposition.
What one should do after a mistake -- the poet's counsel, not to drown in regret. Rejected LO-73: nothing states it outright.
The purport of the whole line about food, honour and revelry -- the poet's claim about a troubled mind. Rejected LO-76, kept for short phrases rather than whole lines.
The benefit of doing work that comes easily -- the poet's proposition. Rejected LO-73: argued, not located.
Which cast of mind the poet urges. Rejected LO-72: his teaching rather than the text's use.
Sense of 'chitt mein khata na paavai' -- glossing a short archaic phrase. Rejected LO-70, kept for whole-line propositions.
